clue.text: Top man in N5 fears enemy kidnaps

definitions.note: N5 is the London postcode of Highbury, old home of Arsenal FC, whose long-serving manager was Arsène Wenger

indicators.note: the words fears enemy hold the six-letter boss captive across their join, so kidnaps signals a run of letters carried inside them

explanation.surface: A football boss in north London is said to fear an enemy snatching someone.
explanation.walkthrough: N5 is the London postcode of Arsenal's old Highbury ground, so the top man there is the manager, Arsène Wenger, in charge from 1996 to 2018.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsène Wenger managed Arsenal, the club based in the N5 postcode, so his first name is the head man there.

clue.text: Adjutant-general and I think we should dangle — they do!

parts.note: AG is the standard abbreviation for an Adjutant-General, a senior army staff officer
let's is the everyday way of proposing that we should do something

explanation.surface: An army officer, keen to hang about, urges his troops to idle with him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: these are the metal tags on laces, also ornamental pendants that dangle from clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglets are the tags on laces or the ornamental pendants on dress, things that hang down and swing.

clue.text: See 13
Brazilian, could it be, lit spinning in microwave?

indicators.note: in places the jumbled word inside the cooking verb

parts.note: to nuke food is slang for cooking it in a microwave oven

indicators.note: something spinning is turned round and round, so the word lit gets jumbled

explanation.surface: A Brazilian wonders whether something lit is turning round inside a microwave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazilian' looks like a person; it is the Brazil nut. To 'nuke' is slang for cooking in a microwave.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazil nut is a kind of nut, so something Brazilian in that sense would resemble a nut.

clue.text: Deviously, it's me caring about a linguistic family

indicators.note: acting deviously means going round about, so the letters of me caring are taken in a roundabout order

explanation.surface: Someone claims their caring is a devious act on behalf of their family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Germanic languages, including English, German and Dutch, form one branch of the Indo-European language family.

clue.text: See 21
See 13
Here's African ready to mount ram

indicators.note: in a down entry, to mount is to climb upwards, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: an Arian is someone born under Aries, the Ram of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An African stands ready to climb onto a ram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for cash ('the ready'), not willingness.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is the currency of Nigeria, so it is African money, and ready is slang for money.

clue.text: Certain to support small business outside Big Apple getting up something very attractive

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting word sits underneath the rest
the company abbreviation goes outside, around the other piece

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: in a down entry getting up means rising, so the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: the Big Apple is New York City, abbreviated NY
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A sure bet backs a small firm outside New York that is rising to become a magnet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'getting up' reads upward and 'to support' means sitting underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynosure is a centre of attention or admiration, originally the Pole Star that sailors watched.

clue.text: Take care of fine tenor locked in little room

indicators.note: being locked in means shut up inside, so the pieces go inside the room

parts.note: the loo is the British word for a toilet, a small room
OK means fine, all right
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A singer is fined after being locked in the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To look to something is to attend to or tend it, as in looking to one's defences.

clue.text: See 26
In communication with rocket

definitions.meaning: British slang for a severe reprimand, as in getting a rocket from the boss

explanation.surface: Someone is in contact with a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in conversation with someone is one sense; a stern telling-off, British 'a rocket', is the other.

clue.text: Coach describes our Olympic team failing to win as 'ruddy habitual characteristic'

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so the coaching word goes around the rest

parts.note: to coach someone is to groom them for a role
the British Olympic team competes as Team GB
failing to win is a loss

explanation.surface: A trainer calls the British Olympic team's failures a 'ruddy' habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' means draws round. 'ruddy' reads as a mild British oath but in the definition means red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: A grog blossom is the red nose or pimply skin of a heavy drinker, a ruddy mark caused by habit.

clue.text: Line from 21 5 version of Hamlet hits top ten — this good!

indicators.note: a new version of something reworks it, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A new version of Hamlet makes the top ten, and it is this good!
explanation.walkthrough: 21 5 is the band R.E.M.; the line comes from their song 'Losing My Religion'.
explanation.definitionFit: The words are a lyric from R.E.M.'s 1991 hit, sung by Michael Stipe.

clue.text: Passes a gambler sees and raises

parts.note: passes, as of time, means goes
a means one
a better is someone who bets

explanation.surface: A poker player passes, and another gambler matches the bet and raises it.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker, to see a bet and raise is to match it and then increase it.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching a stake then adding more is outdoing a rival, the idiom for surpassing someone.

clue.text: One transmitting cross-dressing fact number 1 to the north

parts.note: TV is short for transvestite, a cross-dresser
a stat, short for statistic, is a numerical fact

indicators.note: in a down entry going to the north means upwards, so the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: the Roman numeral I means one

explanation.surface: A broadcaster airs a number-one fact about cross-dressing up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' turns NO and I into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A television station is a broadcaster, an organisation sending out programmes over the air.

clue.text: Roman Catholic burial arrayed in red

indicators.note: to be arrayed is to be set out in order, so the letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: A Catholic burial is held with mourners dressed in red.
explanation.walkthrough: Rubrics, the directions in service books, were traditionally printed in red; 'rubric' comes from the Latin for red.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubrical means relating to rubrics, the liturgical instructions printed in red ink, so it is printed in scarlet.

clue.text: In this state, we can tell dragoons beset neutrals

definitions.text: In this state, we can tell

indicators.note: to dragoon is to coerce or force, so the letters are forced into a new order

explanation.surface: Cavalry soldiers surround neutral parties, who can report what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dragoons' looks like a noun, cavalry troops; it is the verb meaning bullies, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be told or spoken has the quality of being sayable, the state described.

clue.text: The Stalin family footballer in Washington?

definitions.text: The Stalin family footballer in Washington?

parts.words: The Stalin family footballer in Washington?
parts.note: communists such as Stalin are Reds, and their family is their kin; Washington's American football team was long called by this name

explanation.surface: A footballer in Washington is said to belong to Stalin's family.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington's NFL team was formerly the Redskins; Reds is the old nickname for communists, and kin means family.
explanation.definitionFit: A player for Washington's former NFL team was known by the team's singular name.

clue.text: Chosen right old dance music

parts.note: chosen by vote means elect, as in president-elect

explanation.surface: The right sort of old dance music has been picked.
explanation.definitionFit: Electro is a style of electronic dance music that arose in the early 1980s.

clue.text: What shoots dazzlingly out of electricity?

indicators.note: out here sets the short letter outward into the middle of the meter word, a container signal

parts.note: a prepayment electricity meter is what runs out of electricity
O is the abbreviated of, as in o'clock

explanation.surface: Something shoots out of an electrical supply in a dazzling flash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' places O inside METER, the device that measures electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a streak of light from space debris burning up in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Does this falsely represent 'I've one empty dream'?

definitions.text: Does this falsely represent 'I've one empty dream'?

indicators.note: to represent something falsely is to misrender it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether a dream claimed to be empty is being misrepresented.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the band R.E.M., referred to as 21 5 elsewhere in this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: This sleep phase is when vivid dreaming happens, so it would belie a claim of an empty dream.

clue.text: Nasty to peer nursing contempt for Chaucer's ultimate destination

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the jumbled letters cradle the other piece
something nasty is twisted or warped, so the letters of to peer are jumbled

parts.note: scorn means contempt

explanation.surface: A nasty remark to a nobleman hides contempt for Chaucer's final place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' jumbles TO PEER into POETER, which 'nursing' wraps round SCORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer was the first writer buried in this part of Westminster Abbey, his final resting place.

clue.text: Champions League pundits, so to speak, selling themselves?

definitions.text: Champions League pundits, so to speak
definitions.meaning: television pundits discussing a football match are talking about the match being played
British slang for working as a prostitute

explanation.surface: Football pundits on TV are accused of selling out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Champions League is Europe's top club football competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pundits commenting on a match are literally focused on the football; the idiom also means working in prostitution.

clue.text: This office-worker's in to redesign silk screen

indicators.note: redesigning reworks something, so the letters of the printing words are rearranged once the extra word is set aside

explanation.surface: An office worker is brought in to redesign a silk-screen print.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus IN is an anagram of SILK SCREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerkess is a female clerk, chiefly Scottish usage, someone doing office work.

clue.text: 21 5 singer embraces leader of rock band

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the singer's name goes around the other letter

parts.note: Michael Stipe is the lead singer of R.E.M., the 21 5 of the grid

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A singer hugs the frontman of a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like part of 'rock band'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a band of colour or a strip across a surface, two synonyms.

clue.text: Forgoing the theology riling me, sin is rife…

definitions.text: Forgoing the theology riling me, sin is rife…

indicators.note: forgoing means doing without, so the letters of the small word are set aside from the pool
something rife is rampant and spreading wild, so the remaining letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A disillusioned believer gives up on theology, irritated by the abundance of sin.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove THE from THEOLOGY RILING ME SIN and rearrange the rest; the result is R.E.M.'s 1991 song title, which the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning theology and finding sin everywhere is a loss of faith, the song's idiom for exasperation.
